rating_actions_in_window.from: Not previously rated by S&P in window context
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: S&P placed Mississippi Baptist Health System on CreditWatch developing in March 2017 reflecting pending merger with Baptist Memorial Health Care of Memphis.

Mississippi Baptist Health Systems completed merger with Baptist Memorial Health Care (Memphis TN) on 2017-05-01 forming one of largest US non-profit health systems. MBHS standalone bonds either refunded or absorbed into BMHC obligated group; standalone Fitch rating effectively superseded.

fitch._warning: Standalone MBHS rating effectively withdrawn at merger close May 2017. Post-merger, Baptist Memorial parent carried Aa2/Aa rating tier, materially stronger than legacy BBB/Negative MBHS.

outcome_class_rationale: MBHS standalone BBB/Negative rating was effectively terminated at May 1 2017 merger with Baptist Memorial Health Care. From a 2016 BBB obligor perspective this is a credit positive event (absorbed into much stronger parent) — but the standalone Fitch BBB/Negative rating did not survive the window.

operating_metrics_fy2016._warning: FY16 revenue $526M and $3.9M operating loss verified per Jackson Jambalaya local reporting. LTD $97.1M from Series 2007A bonds (Fitch press). DCOH approximated.

_research_notes: Discussion began September 2016, definitive shared-mission-agreement signed late April 2017, merger closed May 1 2017. MBHS was bleeding losses (FY15 -$23.4M, FY16 -$3.9M), driving the deal. Baptist Memorial absorbed all four MBHS hospitals.
